chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man killed a man in the open land (al-Hill), then entered the Sanctuary (al-Haram).' He said, 'He is not killed, nor fed, nor given drink, nor sold, nor given shelter, until he exits the Sanctuary, then the punishment is carried out against him.'

I said, 'What do you say about a man who killed in the Sanctuary or stole?' He said, 'The punishment is carried out against him immediately, for he did not consider the sanctity of the Sanctuary [to be a barrier].'
Allah the Exalted has said, 'So if anyone aggresses against you, attack him with the like of what he attacked you with.'
He said, 'This applies in the Sanctuary.'
Then he said, 'So there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers.'

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary, specifically referring to Mecca or Masjid al-Haram, a place of sacred inviolability.
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land or non-sanctuary area, contrasted with the Haram.
key_terms.فَلَا عُدْوَانَ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِي: Quranic verse indicating that aggression is permissible only against those who transgress.
key_terms.يُقَامَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ: The punishment is carried out against him (specifically hudud penalties).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a criminal who hides in the Haram after committing a crime?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a criminal seeking refuge in the Sanctuary (al-Haram) versus committing a crime within it. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that while the Sanctuary grants temporary immunity from immediate execution to preserve its sanctity, it does not grant impunity; the offender is detained until they exit, at which point the *hadd* is applied. The Imam supports this by citing Quran 2:194 to argue that the 'limit' of retaliation applies within the Sanctuary, while also referencing the principle of 'no hostility except against wrongdoers' to justify the specific treatment of those who violate the Sanctuary's peace.
